issues.spec_citation: SQL injection best practice: quote string literals separately from identifiers before SQL interpolation.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/sources/csv.py:83 builds scan_expr = f"read_csv_auto('{self._path}')" and line 86 executes f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW resources AS {projection}". A contained DuckDB repro with path suffix "'); DROP TABLE sentinel; --" dropped the sentinel table. Proposed safer implementation: import quote_sql_literal and build scan_expr = f"read_csv_auto({quote_sql_literal(self._path)})"; add a regression test mirroring FileSystemSource path escaping.
issues.root_cause: CSVSource bypasses the shared quote_sql_literal() helper used by FileSystemSource and PostgresSource.
issues.resolution: CSVSource.register() now uses quote_sql_literal(self._path) for the read_csv_auto path literal; regression test verifies a malicious filename cannot execute DROP TABLE.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition logical model: parser and public constructor boundaries must preserve validated resource/profile/fhirVersion/where semantics.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/viewdef/types.py:576-580 accepts resource/profile/fhirVersion directly in ViewDefinition.from_dict(), so resource arrays, scalar profile, and unknown fhirVersion values are accepted. fhir4ds/viewdef/types.py:666 stores where directly; fhir4ds/viewdef/generator.py:974-981 then only applies dict entries from list-like root_where, so parser-supported dict/string where inputs from from_dict() are silently ignored. Manual repro accepted resource=['Patient'], profile='http://x', fhirVersion=['bogus'], and generated SQL without the active = true filter. Proposed safer implementation: make from_dict() reuse the same root metadata and where parsing/validation helpers as parse_view_definition(), or delegate public dict construction through parse_view_definition().
issues.root_cause: Public convenience constructor validation drifted from parser.py for root metadata and where fields.
issues.resolution: ViewDefinition.from_dict() delegates through parse_view_definition(), restoring shared validation for root metadata and where normalization.

issues.spec_citation: SQL injection best practice: generated SQL identifiers and aliases must be quoted or validated before interpolation.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/viewdef/join.py:130-145 interpolates pluralized join.resource and join.name directly into generated JOIN SQL; parser.py:247-268 also accepts join.name/resource without SQL-name or ResourceType validation. Even though the main SQLGenerator currently does not integrate joins, generate_join()/JoinGenerator are public surfaces and can emit injectable SQL for malicious ViewDefinition join aliases/resources. Proposed safer implementation: validate join.name with validate_sql_name(), validate join.resource against KNOWN_FHIR_RESOURCE_TYPES, and quote table aliases/table references consistently.
issues.root_cause: Legacy join SQL generation predates the newer ViewDefinition identifier-quoting and ResourceType validation boundaries.
issues.resolution: Join dataclass/parser/generator now validate sql-name aliases and FHIR ResourceType resources, and generated join table/alias identifiers are quoted.
